seoTitle: How to Add a Hyperlink in Jotform Easily
metaDescription: Learn how to insert a clickable hyperlink into a Jotform form in 2026 using the Paragraph element's rich text editor to link out cleanly.
intro: Linking out to terms and conditions, a product catalog, or a downloadable resource is a common need, but Jotform doesn't give hyperlinks their own dedicated field — you build them inside the Paragraph element's rich text editor instead. That's a small distinction that saves a lot of hunting once you know it. This guide walks through adding the Paragraph block, selecting text, inserting the link, and setting it to open in a new tab so you don't pull respondents away from a form they haven't finished.

steps.heading: Open the form you're adding the link to
steps.body: From My Workspace, hover over any form in your list to reveal quick actions like Edit Form, Inbox, and More, or just click the form title to open it directly. This is the jumping-off point regardless of which form needs the link — registration forms, order forms, anything with a Paragraph element already in it or room to add one.

image.caption: My Workspace with a form row expanded to show Edit Form, Inbox, and More — the quickest way into the builder.

steps.heading: Find a spot for the Paragraph element
steps.body: Inside the builder, scroll to where the link should live logically — near a Submit button is common for terms and conditions, but it can go anywhere. The Add Element button in the top-left corner is what opens the sidebar you'll use next; the rest of your fields, like a credit card block or an autocomplete field, stay untouched while you work.

image.caption: A form builder canvas with existing fields and the Add Element button ready to bring in a new Paragraph block.

steps.heading: Drag in a Paragraph element and open the editor
steps.body: Under the Basic tab in Add Element, drag Paragraph onto your canvas wherever you positioned it in the previous step. Double-click the new block to activate its rich text editor — a formatting toolbar appears above the text area with options for bold, alignment, lists, and a chain-link icon for inserting URLs. Type or paste the text you want to make clickable, such as "Click Here to Visit the Website."

steps.heading: Highlight your text and insert the link
steps.body: Select the exact words you want clickable — this matters, because whatever you highlight becomes the anchor text, and anything left unselected stays plain text. With the text highlighted, click the Insert/Edit Link icon in the toolbar to open the link dialog. Only the selected portion turns into a hyperlink, so double-check your selection before clicking through.

image.caption: The rich text editor toolbar with "Click Here To Visit the Website" selected, ready for the Insert/Edit Link icon.

steps.heading: Paste the URL and set it to open in a new tab
steps.body: In the link dialog, paste the full destination URL, including https://, and look for the target setting — switch it from the default to "Open in new window" so clicking the link doesn't navigate the respondent away from an in-progress form. Skipping this step is the single most common mistake with Jotform hyperlinks, since the default behavior can cost you a partially completed submission.

steps.heading: Match the link's styling to your form
steps.body: Back in the toolbar, use the text color and formatting options to make the link visually consistent with the rest of your form's branding rather than leaving it in whatever default blue the editor applies. This is optional but worth the extra thirty seconds — a hyperlink that clashes with your color scheme reads as an afterthought.

steps.heading: Save your changes and test the live link
steps.body: Save the paragraph block, then use Preview Form to click the link exactly as a respondent would. Confirm it opens in a new tab and loads the correct destination, then check the same thing on a mobile-width preview, since tap targets on rich text links can behave differently on smaller screens than they do in the desktop editor.

faq.question: Can I style the hyperlink to match my form's color scheme?
faq.answer: Yes, the rich text editor lets you apply inline styling to your linked text so it matches your form's overall brand colors.

faq.question: Will the hyperlink open in the same window by default?
faq.answer: By default it may open in the same window, so it's worth explicitly setting the target property to a new tab if you don't want users to lose their form progress.

faq.question: Can I link to a downloadable file instead of a webpage?
faq.answer: Yes, as long as you have a direct URL to the file, you can paste it into the link field the same way as any other web link.

faq.question: Is there a limit to how many hyperlinks I can add to one form?
faq.answer: There's no strict limit, but adding too many links inside a single Paragraph element can clutter the form's design and confuse respondents.
